geo-strat-01-c1.text: University of California Museum of Paleontology. Nicolaus Steno (1638-1686). UCMP Berkeley.
geo-strat-01-c1.claim: In 1669 Nicolaus Steno set out the foundational rule of stratigraphy.

geo-strat-01-c1.text: University of California Museum of Paleontology. Nicolaus Steno (1638-1686). UCMP Berkeley, Understanding Science / History of Life.
geo-strat-01-c1.quote: layers of rock are arranged in a time sequence, with the oldest on the bottom and the youngest on the top
geo-strat-01-c1.claim: In any undisturbed sequence of rock layers (strata), the oldest layers are at the bottom and the youngest are at the top.

geo-strat-01-c2.text: University of California Museum of Paleontology. Nicolaus Steno (1638-1686). UCMP Berkeley.
geo-strat-01-c2.quote: rock layers form in the horizontal position
geo-strat-01-c2.claim: Original horizontality means sediment layers are deposited horizontally, so strata you find tilted or folded were deformed after deposition.

geo-strat-01-c3.text: National Park Service. Geologic Principles: Cross-Cutting Relationships. nps.gov.
geo-strat-01-c3.quote: Other similar relationships include faults being younger than the rock layers they cut...
geo-strat-01-c3.claim: any geological feature (a fault, an igneous intrusion, an erosion surface) that cuts across existing rock layers must be younger than the layers it cuts.
